### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/rest`, `@objectstack/runtime`, touching **22** documentable anchor(s).

**26** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 70cfb12771bc8cc44bff830ea7528714f14d715e`.

⛔ **10** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **39** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 70cfb12771bc8cc44bff830ea7528714f14d715e` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `d1a14284cab408295948b9af76648b16a75b8163` — the merge of head `81e9289baa3466f31285059cc907e133b4789953` into base `70cfb12771bc8cc44bff830ea7528714f14d715e`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin d1a14284cab408295948b9af76648b16a75b8163 && git checkout d1a14284cab408295948b9af76648b16a75b8163
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 70cfb12771bc8cc44bff830ea7528714f14d715e 81e9289baa3466f31285059cc907e133b4789953 && git checkout -B drift-repro 70cfb12771bc8cc44bff830ea7528714f14d715e && git merge --no-ff 81e9289baa3466f31285059cc907e133b4789953

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 70cfb12771bc8cc44bff830ea7528714f14d715e
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 70cfb12771bc8cc44bff830ea7528714f14d715e` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `81e9289baa3466f31285059cc907e133b4789953`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.lookup-artifact-item-call-sites.test.ts, packages/objectql/src/package-disable-enforcement.test.ts, packages/rest/src/meta-item-read-gate.ts, packages/rest/src/meta-item-read-gate.object-package-disabled.test.ts, packages/rest/src/rest-exposure-gate-one-object-read.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/meta.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/meta-object-disabled-package.test.ts + packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts (the item read's cached, uncached and draft arms, `serveMetaItemLayered`, `/published`, `fetchCurrentMetaDocument` and `gatesPerCaller`, `enforceApiAccess`, the import-template and reference-label reads), packages/rest/src/error-response.ts, packages/types/src/thrown-http-error.ts, packages/types/src/data-error-classification.ts, packages/objectql/src/registry.ts (`isPackageDisabled`, `isObjectPackageDisabled`), packages/spec/src/api/error-code-ledger.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/contracts/objectql-engine.ts, packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/organization-ownership.ts, packages/cli/src/utils/organization-ownership-apply.ts, packages/cli/src/utils/organization-ownership-plan.ts, packages/rest/src/import-prepare.ts, packages/rest/src/data-action-routes.ts, packages/core/src/utils/import-runner.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/connector-pull.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-plugin.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/admin-import-users.ts, .changeset/24040-reseed-converted-body.md, .changeset/pre/24031-exposure-gate-one-object-read.md, scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs, scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs; the three `.changeset/24097-*.md` read as prose; objectui at 2ec9e2a read-only (FormPage.tsx, MetadataProvider.tsx, AiChatPage.tsx, MetadataService.ts, PackagesPage.tsx)

### ① Derived judgments

Read at the head; the check-runs' conclusions are the gate verdicts (40 runs: 34 success, 6 skipped, none failed or in progress).

1. **Every by-name object face refuses with the data plane's envelope — right.** `getMetaItem` folds the type first (`canonicalizeMetaRequestType`, so the plural `objects` lands on the same check), asks `isObjectOfDisabledPackage(this.engine?.registry, name)` and throws `objectPackageDisabledError(name)` before `readMetaItem` runs, so the active read, `state: 'draft'` and `previewDrafts` are refused before any layer is read. `getMetaItemLayered` (`?layers=true`, `/layers`) carries the same check after its own canonicalisation and before the code layer. `assertObjectRegistered` now throws through the same constructor, so `code`, `status`, `object` and message have one source. RestServer: the cached arm (`getMetaItemCached` delegates to `getMetaItem`, its catch rethrows), the uncached arm and the draft arm all let the throw reach the route's catch, where `thrownAnswerIsBareNotFound` is false (the resolved code is `OBJECT_PACKAGE_DISABLED`, a ledger code, never `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`), so `handleRouteError` → `resolveErrorResponse` → pass-through renders status 404 with `code: OBJECT_PACKAGE_DISABLED` (`resolveThrownHttpError` keeps a ledger-registered code as `code`; `demotedDeclaredCode` demotes nothing); RestServer has no registry fallback on these routes. Runtime dispatcher: `readFromProtocol` rethrows that one code instead of falling through, the registry-first path is skipped when `isObjectPackageDisabled(name)` answers true, and the draft arm (`readPendingDraft`) and layered arm (`answerMetaLayered`) render through `errorFromThrown`; pinned on both kernels through `HttpDispatcher.dispatch`, with `registry.getObject` asserted never called for the disabled name.
   Still serving, named and not fixed, outside the ruling's fence: `GET /meta/:type/:name/published` on both transports (the layered read sits in a try whose catch falls through to the published snapshot — confirmed in code, as the PR's acceptance note says); and on the dispatcher only, the one-segment legacy spelling `GET /meta/NAME` (`registry.getObject(typeOrName)` after the list misses, meta.ts line 2165 at head) and the `/meta/object/:name/state/:field` FSM read (line 1026): registry reads on API doors, the class ruling item 3 closed for the object branch. Carried in ③.

2. **Resolution readers and the authoring caller — right.** `registry.getObject` and `registry.listItems('object')` are untouched and stay pinned `enforces: false`. `saveMetaItem`'s destructive-change prior read now calls `this.readMetaItem` inside the try whose catch rethrows only `DESTRUCTIVE_CHANGE`, so a field drop on a disabled package's object still answers `409 DESTRUCTIVE_CHANGE`: pinned on code, status and the stored row keeping the field, and ablation (c) turns that pin red when the read points back at the API face. `readMetaItem` makes no call back into `getMetaItem`. The seed adapter and build probes keep reading the API face on purpose (best-effort, swallowed).

3. **Checked before any layer, healthy package unaffected — right.** In both `getMetaItem` and `getMetaItemLayered` the order is canonicalise → refuse → read. Controls are pinned (`healthy_widget` served by name and layered; the runtime pin's control served on both kernels) and measured over HTTP (`crm_account` 200 with the probe package disabled). The runtime's registry-first skip uses the same predicate, so a healthy object answers from the registry as before.

4. **No widening — right.** `readMetaItem` is `private`; `objectPackageDisabledError` and `isObjectOfDisabledPackage` are module-local, not exported; `OBJECT_PACKAGE_DISABLED` already sits in the error-code ledger; no spec key and no `packages/spec` edit (the runtime reads the predicate through a local optional type because `EngineSchemaRegistryView` declares `getPackage` and `disablePackage` but not `isObjectPackageDisabled`); `loadObjectItem`'s signature is unchanged and its new arm returns `undefined` for one code. Accept sets only narrow: the exposure gate passing a disabled package's object on cannot admit a request, because every data verb funnels through `assertObjectRegistered`, the same predicate on the same registry.

5. **The flipped `rest-exposure-gate-one-object-read` row — right and consistent.** The card said the gate "inherits that with no REST change"; ruling item 4 orders the refusal read as no object without the fail-open warn; the #24031 changeset's move is reversed and the new rest changeset states the FROM → TO. The pin runs a real `ObjectStackProtocolImplementation` on a real `SchemaRegistry`, so the row exercises the new refusal rather than a mock; it asserts 404 + `OBJECT_PACKAGE_DISABLED` with `createData` reached once, and the ALLOWED row is unchanged. `loadObjectItem` has one consumer (`enforceApiAccess`), so the "no object" reading reaches nothing else.

6. **Refusal pins assert `code` + `status` — right.** The envelope case asserts `code`, `status`, `object` and message identity with `assertObjectRegistered`'s throw; `servesByName` counts only `OBJECT_PACKAGE_DISABLED` as refusing and rethrows anything else, so `NO_DRAFT` cannot pass for enforcement (the seed adds a pending draft so the draft row serves before the disable); the REST and runtime pins assert code + status; the warn-suppression pin keeps the "any other throw still warns once" half.

Residue, not a defect: the by-name predicate is the data plane's (`registry.isObjectPackageDisabled`, owner-based through `resolveObjectKey`) while the list filters by each served item's `_packageId`; they agree for a registered object, which is the one predicate the ruling ordered.

### ② Semver level

- `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`: `minor`, BREAKING banner, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, adr-0087 marker `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` — matches the diff: a served-set narrowing of a public read door; no stored shape, key, export or code added or removed. `check-changeset-no-major` reads a declared narrowing as BREAKING shipped `minor` in the launch window (the #24040 convention cited). Right.
- `@objectstack/runtime`: the same triple — matches: the dispatcher's object door narrows, nothing else published changes. Right.
- `@objectstack/rest`: the same triple — right, conservatively labelled. The diff publishes a refusal-code move (405 / 404 `OBJECT_API_*` back to 404 `OBJECT_PACKAGE_DISABLED` for an already-refused request) and a warn log that stops; the accept set is unchanged, and #24031 shipped the inverse move as `patch` with `Clause-②: no`. Declaring a consumer-visible code change BREAKING is at least as strict as owed, the body says "a refusal moves" honestly, and the gate accepted it.
- `@objectstack/objectql`: no changeset; its diff is one test file outside the published files. Right.
- The three dispositions were re-verified by `Check Changeset` (success). Each body's "What changes for you" names a remedy (re-enable the package), not a rewrite prescription.

### ③ Boundary flags

Report 6238493670, every entry:
- deviation 1 (pin sweep: the #24031 row flipped; the `lookupArtifactItem` ledger re-keyed `getMetaItem` → `readMetaItem` with the same sites, arguments and dispositions) — answered in ① 5 and read in the diff. Right.
- deviation 2 (runtime local type for the predicate; `packages/spec` out of fence) — answered: the view type lacks the member; the optional call mirrors the protocol's own posture; no widening.
- deviation 3 (commit ae7c051d titled narrower than its content, history not rewritten) — cosmetic; one landing.
- deviation 4 (shared clone deepened so two derived gates could run) — process, additive; not a contract matter.
- deviation 5 (attribution per AGENTS.md over the harness reminder) — process; noted.
- deviation 6 (no objectql changeset) — answered in ②.
- open question 1 (bump level) — answered in ②. open question 2 (predicate typing) — answered above.
- out-of-scope 1 (`GET /meta/app/NAME` of a disabled package answers 200 while the list omits it, measured over HTTP) — escalated to the seat: ruling item 7 has the seat file the family card for the non-object types; ⛔ not this PR's.
- out-of-scope 2 (`/published` serves the snapshot of a disabled package's object; carrier none) — confirmed in code on both transports; escalated: an API door still serving, outside the ruling's fence, needs a carrier — the same family card (one answer per door), not a rider here. The two dispatcher registry reads named in ① 1 (one-segment legacy spelling; `/state/:field`) go on that card too. `/history`, `/audit` and `/diff` are unaffected for objects: `gatesPerCaller('object')` is false, so `fetchCurrentMetaDocument` never reads an object.
- out-of-scope 3 (the consumed #24031 changeset states the opposite) — answered: consumed changesets are release-owned; the new rest changeset carries the FROM → TO.
- Ruling item 6, measured not edited — confirmed in code: `lock.verdict` is asked only for rows `readMetadataKeyRows` selects (`type IN PRESENTATIONAL_TYPES`: view, dashboard, report, translation, email_template) and for `'position'`; the refusal is `type === 'object'` only, so `packages/cli` is rightly untouched.
- Report 6236347492's carried findings (the runtime registry fallback; the fail-open warn) are closed by ruling items 3 and 4 as implemented here.
- For the ledger's owner, not this PR (`packages/spec` is fenced): the `OBJECT_PACKAGE_DISABLED` row's comment still reads "data plane refuses"; the by-name `/meta` reads now raise it too.
- `main` has moved in `protocol.ts` since the merge base 7d6ec91d2 (+74/−25, other cards); the claim already says whichever lands later merges `main`.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-24097-meta-by-name-disabled-package`
Reviewed-by: `session_01JtSQQ3EWsbNPzyYMug1tXy`

**VERDICT: PASS**
